_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); gold-miner signals with Newmont's rule-T thresholds

pit_profile.why: 'Newmont is one of the world’s largest gold producers and is the only gold company included in the S&P 500 Index and the Fortune 500, and was the first gold company included in the Dow Jones Sustainability Index-World.' 'Our business is dependent on the prices of gold and copper, which fluctuate on a daily basis and are affected by numerous factors beyond our control.' 'A substantial or extended decline in gold or copper prices would have a material adverse effect on Newmont.' (the FY2010 10-K's own words; it does not call the business cyclical, so DURABLE, the MU rule)

classification.quality_note: 'Newmont is one of the world’s largest gold producers and is the only gold company included in the S&P 500 Index and the Fortune 500, and was the first gold company included in the Dow Jones Sustainability Index-World.' 'Our business is dependent on the prices of gold and copper, which fluctuate on a daily basis and are affected by numerous factors beyond our control.' 'A substantial or extended decline in gold or copper prices would have a material adverse effect on Newmont.' (the FY2010 10-K's own words; it does not call the business cyclical, so DURABLE, the MU rule). durable franchise (obsolescence risk 2/5); price cheap; Ratio B 0.11x; -43% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap +1.15; conservative 2yr +151%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -36.2%/yr (worst year FY02-FY10 ex-FY07, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +2.1%/yr (Q3 revenue YoY + margin + buyback); P/E at its 9.9-yr ex-FY07 median

BULL.desc: EPS +41.3%/yr (FY02-FY10 ex-FY07 CAGR, at least BASE); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +80.0%/yr (best 2-yr run FY02-FY10 ex-FY07, at least BULL); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: NEM (retrospective, 2011-11-18) ◉ BUY — Ratio B 0.11x (64.4% downside to Bear $23.31 / +599.3% upside to Bull $457.74) | Adj composite 2.15 vs market 1.00: gap +1.15 [UNDERVALUED] | -43% above the EPP floor $115.25 (25x FY11E $4.61) | Conservative 2-yr case: +151.4% total (+75.7%/yr) | At 14.2x FY11E the 15% hurdle price $86.57 sits at or below the BASE case; revenue +5.7% YoY in Q3 2011, forward revenues +5.7% (Q3 2011 revenue growth (no revenue guide)); no disruption theme has dated evidence.
